title: The Coming Battles Over American Foreign Policy
author: Kori Schake
text: Podcast The Coming Battles Over American Foreign PolicyA Conversation With Kori Schake and Thomas Wright Published on November 5, 2026 Play Listen to the Episode 67 minutes 00:00 / 1:06:31 0.5×1×1.5×2× MP3 Close audio player Print Print this article Save Sign in and save to read later Close Share The Coming Battles Over American Foreign Policy A Conversation With Kori Schake and Thomas Wright Share in email Share on Facebook Share on X Share on LinkedIn Article link: https://www.foreignaffairs.com/podcasts/coming-battles-over-american-foreign-policyhttps://www.foreignaffairs.com/podcasts/coming-battles-over-american-foreign-policy Request reprint permissions here.Episode Details The Democrats’ sweeping victory in the midterm elections this week marks not only the start of a new phase for Donald Trump’s foreign policy. It also kicks off a more intensive discussion among both Democrats and Republicans about the future of American foreign policy beyond Trump.Dan Kurtz-Phelan spoke with two foreign policy veterans who have participated in these debates inside and outside government, including in Foreign Affairs. Kori Schake, the director of foreign and defense policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, served in the State Department and on the National Security Council under George W. Bush. Tom Wright was senior director for strategic planning at the National Security Council under Joe Biden and is now a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution.All of these debates will have to contend with big questions about specific policies, from China and the Middle East to AI and defense spending. They also involve deep and often bitter fissures between and within parties. Meanwhile, the war in Iran is far from resolved and the specter of an already unpredictable president’s lame-duck period introduces even more uncertainty about what the world will look like when Trump leaves the White House for good in January 2029.Sources:“Dispensable Nation” by Kori Schake“The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy” by Thomas Wright“The Age of Forever Wars” by Lawrence D. FreedmanThis episode of The Foreign Affairs Interview was produced by Adrian Feinberg, Adelaide Parker, Ben Metzner and Kanishk Tharoor, with audio engineering by Todd Yeager and original music by Robin Hilton.
